question.worked_solution:
We will use the fact that the dot product is linear.

To quickly compute the numerator $3u\cdot v,$ we multiply $u\cdot v$ by $3.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(3u)\cdot v & =3(u\cdot v) \\  & =3\cdot 22 \\  & =66.\end{aligned}
$$

To quickly compute the denominator $u\cdot (2u),$ we compute $u\cdot u$ first and then multiply the result by $2.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot (2u) & =2(u\cdot u) \\  & =2({u}_{1}^{2}+{u}_{2}^{2}+{u}_{3}^{2}+{u}_{4}^{2}) \\  & =2({2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{5}^{2}) \\  & =2(4+1+9+25) \\  & =2\cdot 39 \\  & =78.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{(3u)\cdot v}{u\cdot (2u)}=\frac{66}{78}=\frac{11}{13}.
$$
